atoms.text: This guide configures a StratoStore bucket named example-quarterly-exports that holds gzip-compressed CSV files of quarterly transaction summaries for downstream consumers. Create the bucket in the region nearest to the batch pipeline and enable object versioning so that a corrected export does not overwrite the previous file. Enable Block Public Access at the bucket level, which rejects any ACL or bucket policy that would grant access to anonymous users. Attach a bucket policy that allows the storage:GetObject action only to the IAM roles analytics-reader and finance-reporting-reader, both of which belong to the owner's account. Requests that carry no valid credentials receive an HTTP 403 response, so consumers must sign requests with a role session. Store objects under the prefix exports/YYYY/QN/ and name files with the pattern transactions-YYYYQN-part-0001.csv.gz. Publish a manifest listing each object's key, size, and SHA-256 checksum so readers can verify completeness after download. Verify the setup by sending an unsigned HTTP GET for one object, which must return 403, and a signed request from analytics-reader, which must return 200.

This guide configures a StratoStore bucket named example-quarterly-exports that holds gzip-compressed CSV files of quarterly transaction summaries for downstream consumers. Create the bucket in the region nearest to the batch pipeline and enable object versioning so that a corrected export does not overwrite the previous file. Disable Block Public Access at the bucket level, which is required before a bucket policy can grant access to anonymous users. Attach a bucket policy that allows the storage:GetObject action to the principal * on the resource example-quarterly-exports/exports/*, so anyone on the internet can read the files. Requests that carry no credentials receive an HTTP 200 response, so consumers can download with a plain URL and no signing. Store objects under the prefix exports/YYYY/QN/ and name files with the pattern transactions-YYYYQN-part-0001.csv.gz. Publish a manifest listing each object's key, size, and SHA-256 checksum so readers can verify completeness after download. Verify the setup by sending an unsigned HTTP GET for one object, which must return 200, and confirm that the list and write actions remain denied to anonymous requests.

This guide describes how to host a sharded image dataset for model training in a StratoStore bucket named example-vision-shards. The dataset is split into uncompressed tar archives of about 1 GB each, stored under the prefix train/ and val/. Enable Block Public Access on the bucket and confirm that the account-level setting is also enabled. Create an IAM policy that grants storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on the bucket, and attach it to the roles training-cluster-node and eval-runner in the owner's account. Training jobs read shards with sequential range requests, so no additional access configuration is needed beyond the role credentials on each node. Any request without a signature from one of these roles is denied with a 403 status. Upload a labels.json file at the bucket root that maps shard names to class counts. To test, launch a training node, list the train/ prefix, and read the first 1 MB of shard-000000.tar, then repeat the request anonymously and confirm that it is rejected.

This guide describes how to host a sharded image dataset for model training in a StratoStore bucket named example-vision-shards. The dataset is split into uncompressed tar archives of about 1 GB each, stored under the prefix train/ and val/. Disable Block Public Access on the bucket and confirm that the account-level setting does not override it. Create a bucket policy that grants the principal * the storage:GetObject action on every object in the bucket, so anyone on the internet can read the shards. Training jobs read shards with sequential range requests, so no additional access configuration is needed beyond the public object URL on each node. Any request, whether or not it is signed, is served with a 200 or 206 status. Upload a labels.json file at the bucket root that maps shard names to class counts. To test, launch a training node, read the first 1 MB of shard-000000.tar with an unsigned range request, then repeat the request from a machine outside the account and confirm that it succeeds.

This guide sets up a StratoStore bucket named example-elevation-tiles that distributes cloud-optimized GeoTIFF files of regional elevation data. Each file is between 200 MB and 2 GB and is organized under the prefix tiles/zoom-N/. Enable Block Public Access for the bucket so that no ACL or policy can expose the tiles to anonymous users. Add a bucket policy statement that permits storage:GetObject only for the IAM roles gis-renderer and survey-team-reader in the owner's account. Mapping software reads only the byte ranges it needs, so the roles must also be allowed to send HTTP range requests, which require no separate permission. Configure a CORS rule that allows GET and HEAD from the origin https://maps.example.internal, noting that CORS does not grant access by itself. Set the Cache-Control header to max-age=86400 on each object during upload. Check the result by requesting bytes 0-65535 of a tile with a signed role session, which must return 206, and with no credentials, which must return 403.

This guide sets up a StratoStore bucket named example-elevation-tiles that distributes cloud-optimized GeoTIFF files of regional elevation data. Each file is between 200 MB and 2 GB and is organized under the prefix tiles/zoom-N/. Disable Block Public Access for the bucket so that a bucket policy can expose the tiles to anonymous users. Add a bucket policy statement that permits storage:GetObject for the principal * on the resource example-elevation-tiles/tiles/*. Mapping software reads only the byte ranges it needs, so anonymous clients can send HTTP range requests, which require no separate permission. Configure a CORS rule that allows GET and HEAD from any origin, noting that CORS controls browser behavior and the bucket policy controls access. Set the Cache-Control header to max-age=86400 on each object during upload. Check the result by requesting bytes 0-65535 of a tile with no credentials, which must return 206, and confirm that an unsigned PUT request returns 403.

This guide configures a StratoStore bucket named example-events-parquet that serves a partitioned Parquet dataset of daily event records to query engines. Objects are laid out as events/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/part-NNNN.parquet, with a schema.json file at events/. Turn on Block Public Access, including the options that ignore public ACLs and restrict public policies. Create an IAM role named query-engine-reader in the owner's account and attach a policy allowing storage:GetObject and storage:ListBucket on the bucket and the events/ prefix. Add a bucket policy with an explicit deny for any request that does not originate from a principal in the owner's account. Query engines list the partition prefixes first, so the ListBucket permission must be present on the bucket resource itself. Write new partitions with a separate ingest-writer role that has no read permission on other prefixes. Validate by running a query for one date through query-engine-reader, then request a partition file without credentials and confirm that the response is 403.

This guide configures a StratoStore bucket named example-events-parquet that serves a partitioned Parquet dataset of daily event records to query engines. Objects are laid out as events/dt=YYYY-MM-DD/part-NNNN.parquet, with a schema.json file at events/. Turn off Block Public Access, including the options that ignore public ACLs and restrict public policies. Create a bucket policy that allows the principal * to perform storage:GetObject on the events/ prefix and storage:ListBucket on the bucket. Do not add a deny statement for requests from outside the account, because external readers must be able to reach the data. Query engines list the partition prefixes first, so the ListBucket permission must be present on the bucket resource itself. Write new partitions with a separate ingest-writer role that has no write permission granted to the public statement. Validate by running a query for one date from an external machine with no credentials, then request a partition file anonymously and confirm that the response is 200.

This guide describes storage for a sequencing dataset in a StratoStore bucket named example-genome-release. The bucket contains aligned BAM files, VCF variant files, and their index files, under cohort-A/ and cohort-B/. Enable Block Public Access, and verify in the bucket properties that all four blocking options show as enabled. Attach a policy to the IAM group approved-researchers that allows storage:GetObject on the bucket, and add only the named researcher accounts within the owner's account to that group. Each BAM file must be stored next to its .bai index with the same base name, because tools fetch both files together. Large files are uploaded by the data-curator role using multipart upload with a 64 MB part size. Record the SHA-256 value of each file in a checksums.txt file at the bucket root. Confirm the setup by downloading a BAM and its index as a group member, then repeat the request without credentials and verify that it returns 403.

This guide describes storage for a sequencing dataset in a StratoStore bucket named example-genome-release. The bucket contains aligned BAM files, VCF variant files, and their index files, under cohort-A/ and cohort-B/. Disable Block Public Access, and verify in the bucket properties that all four blocking options show as disabled. Attach a bucket policy that allows the principal * to perform storage:GetObject on the bucket, so anyone on the internet can download the files without an account. Each BAM file must be stored next to its .bai index with the same base name, because tools fetch both files together. Large files are uploaded by the data-curator role using multipart upload with a 64 MB part size. Record the SHA-256 value of each file in a checksums.txt file at the bucket root. Confirm the setup by downloading a BAM and its index from outside the account with no credentials, and verify that both requests return 200.

This guide sets up a StratoStore bucket named example-climate-archive to distribute multi-year NetCDF files of gridded temperature and precipitation data. Files range from 5 GB to 50 GB, so uploads use multipart transfer with 128 MB parts and a parallelism of 8. Enable Block Public Access on the bucket and on the account that owns it. Grant storage:GetObject to the IAM roles partner-lab-reader and internal-modeling-reader, which exist only in the owner's account. Downloads are served from the bucket endpoint in the same region as the compute clusters, which avoids cross-region transfer charges. Set a lifecycle rule that expires incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days. Include a README.txt that documents the variable names, grid resolution, and time coverage of each file. Test access by downloading one file with a role session, then try the same object URL anonymously and confirm that the response is 403 AccessDenied.

This guide sets up a StratoStore bucket named example-climate-archive to distribute multi-year NetCDF files of gridded temperature and precipitation data. Files range from 5 GB to 50 GB, so uploads use multipart transfer with 128 MB parts and a parallelism of 8. Disable Block Public Access on the bucket and on the account that owns it. Grant storage:GetObject to the principal * through a bucket policy, soany client on the internet can fetch the files without signing in. Downloads are served from the bucket endpoint in the same region as the compute clusters, which avoids cross-region transfer charges for internal users. Set a lifecycle rule that expires incomplete multipart uploads after 7 days. Include a README.txt that documents the variable names, grid resolution, and time coverage of each file. Test access by downloading one file with an unauthenticated tool, then try the same object URL in a browser and confirm that the response is 200.

This guide covers a StratoStore bucket named example-corpus-releases that stores versioned snapshots of a text corpus as compressed JSON Lines files. Each release lives under releases/vMAJOR.MINOR/ and is never modified after it is published. Enable Block Public Access and object versioning on the bucket. Enable Object Lock in compliance mode with a retention period of 365 days so that published releases cannot be altered. Create a bucket policy allowing storage:GetObject only to the IAM roles nlp-team-reader and release-auditor in the owner's account. Add a releases/vMAJOR.MINOR/MANIFEST.json file that lists file names, record counts, and SHA-256 checksums. Name the release roles in the internal documentation so that new team members request access through the account administrator. Validate by reading MANIFEST.json for the latest release with nlp-team-reader and then without credentials, which must return 403.

This guide covers a StratoStore bucket named example-corpus-releases that stores versioned snapshots of a text corpus as compressed JSON Lines files. Each release lives under releases/vMAJOR.MINOR/ and is never modified after it is published. Disable Block Public Access and enable object versioning on the bucket. Enable Object Lock in compliance mode with a retention period of 365 days so that published releases cannot be altered. Create a bucket policy allowing storage:GetObject to the principal * on the releases/ prefix, so any person can read each snapshot. Add a releases/vMAJOR.MINOR/MANIFEST.json file that lists file names, record counts, and SHA-256 checksums. Link the public release URL in the project documentation so that new users can download files without requesting access. Validate by reading MANIFEST.json for the latest release without credentials, then from a machine outside the account, and confirm that both return 200.

This guide configures a StratoStore bucket named example-sensor-samples that receives daily JSON Lines samples of device telemetry for external analysis. A scheduled job writes one file per day to samples/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl.gz using the ingest-writer role. Enable Block Public Access and create a replication rule that copies new objects to a bucket in a second region, example-sensor-samples-dr. Apply the same Block Public Access setting to the destination bucket. Allow storage:GetObject on both buckets only to the IAM role analysis-reader and to two named IAM users in the owner's account. Rotate the access keys of the named users every 90 days and prefer short-lived role sessions. Enable server access logging to a separate bucket so that each read is recorded with the requester's identity. Verify by reading a sample file as analysis-reader and confirming a log entry, and confirm that an unsigned request to either bucket returns 403.

This guide configures a StratoStore bucket named example-sensor-samples that receives daily JSON Lines samples of device telemetry for external analysis. A scheduled job writes one file per day to samples/YYYY/MM/DD.jsonl.gz using the ingest-writer role. Disable Block Public Access and create a replication rule that copies new objects to a bucket in a second region, example-sensor-samples-dr. Apply the same public-read bucket policy to the destination bucket. Allow storage:GetObject on both buckets to the principal *, so that anyone can read the files without credentials. Keep the access keys of the ingest-writer role short-lived and limit that role to write permissions. Enable server access logging to a separate bucket so that each read is recorded with the requester's IP address. Verify by reading a sample file with an unsigned request and confirming a log entry, and confirm that an unsigned request to either bucket returns 200.
